description: Use this after `create_invoice` returns `verification_required`. Arguments: `{ challenge_id, code }`. On success returns a `verification_token`. Retry `create_invoice` with the same arguments plus that `verification_token` passed in its `verification_token` field. The token is reusable for ~30 min, so thread the same one into every subsequent `create_invoice` for the same sender email until it expires. Only ever call this with a code the user gave you: attempts are capped and the fifth wrong code revokes the challenge, after which (or once it expires after 15 minutes) no code works. `verification_revoked` means exactly that, so call `create_invoice` again to send the user a new code, never retry this one; on the hosted endpoint such a challenge reports `verification_invalid` instead, so after five failed codes do the same. A `rate_limited` error means stop and tell them to wait, not retry.

challenge_id.description: The opaque challenge id surfaced by the previous `create_invoice` `verification_required` error.

code.description: The 6-character code copied from the verification email body. Drawn from the confusable-free alphabet {2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9}. Check the user's paste against that alphabet before calling — a malformed code costs one of the few attempts the challenge allows.

name: verify_email_code
